name: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations
description: Assesses the seven Cloud Foundations capabilities defined in the AWS Well-Architected Framework: multi-account environment, identity and access management, central observability management, resource and inventory management, security and compliance, cloud financial management, and networking and connectivity. Use this lens to review the organizational-level controls and shared services your foundation team maintains across your AWS environment.

questions.title: How do you structure and govern multiple accounts across teams and environments?
questions.description: A well-structured multi-account environment uses accounts as strong isolation boundaries. Evaluate whether your organizational structure, baseline automation, and lifecycle controls match the security and operational needs of your teams and workloads.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations – Multi-Account Environment (FND01)

choices.title: FND01-BP01: Establish management account and organizational structure

helpfulResource.displayText: The management account is used only for governance. AWS Organizations OUs are structured around security and operational boundaries, not the org chart. Administrative capabilities are delegated to member accounts wherever the service supports it.

improvementPlan.displayText: Move all production workloads out of the management account. Redesign your OU structure to reflect security and lifecycle boundaries rather than reporting lines. Enable delegated administrator for services such as AWS Security Hub, AWS Config, and AWS IAM Identity Center.

choices.title: FND01-BP02: Establish ownership for billing, security, and operations

helpfulResource.displayText: Every account and significant resource has a current named owner for billing, security, and operational response recorded as a role or team (not an individual) in account and resource metadata so automation and incident response can rely on it.

improvementPlan.displayText: Update account alternate contacts to distribution lists or role-based aliases. Enforce ownership tags at provisioning time using AWS Organizations tag policies and Service Control Policies.

choices.title: FND01-BP03: Establish boundaries and scopes for your environments

helpfulResource.displayText: Experimentation, pre-production, and production sit in clearly separated environments with progressively tighter access restrictions, expressed as permission sets in IAM Identity Center, so teams can test without endangering production.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define distinct OUs or account groupings for sandbox, development, staging, and production. Apply progressively restrictive SCPs as workloads move toward production. Validate that controls are consistent across all lifecycle environments.

choices.title: FND01-BP04: Establish a strategy for experimental and temporary environments

helpfulResource.displayText: A first-class path exists for experimentation and short-lived work so teams are not forced to test in shared development accounts or stand up shadow accounts outside governance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create a sandbox OU with vended accounts, spending limits, and auto-cleanup policies. Provide self-service account vending so teams can provision and decommission experimental environments without bypassing governance.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the multi-account environment best practices are currently implemented.

questions.title: How do you manage identities, enforce least privilege, and protect access to accounts and resources?
questions.description: Strong identity controls protect your cloud environment while enabling the business to move at speed. Evaluate whether you have centralized identity, protected privileged accounts, enforced least privilege, established data perimeters, and maintained credentials over time.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations – Identity and Access Management (FND02)

choices.title: FND02-BP01: Protect account root users and establish alternate contacts

helpfulResource.displayText: Root users are protected with hardware MFA, monitored for use, and used only by exception. Alternate contacts for every account point to distribution lists rather than individuals.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable hardware MFA on every account root user. Set up AWS Organizations policies to alert on root usage. Replace individual alternate contacts with shared distribution lists or role-based aliases.

choices.title: FND02-BP02: Use strong sign-in mechanisms

helpfulResource.displayText: MFA is enforced on all human identities, especially privileged ones. Password policies meet or exceed current standards and are enforced by the identity provider.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enforce MFA for all IAM Identity Center users, particularly those with elevated permissions. Configure the identity provider to require phishing-resistant MFA factors (e.g., FIDO2) for privileged roles.

choices.title: FND02-BP03: Employ a centralized identity provider

helpfulResource.displayText: Workforce identity is centralized and AWS access flows by federation from a single authoritative source that synchronises joiner, mover, and leaver changes automatically.

improvementPlan.displayText: Integrate AWS IAM Identity Center with your corporate identity provider (e.g., Entra ID, Okta). Eliminate direct IAM user accounts used for human access. Automate provisioning and deprovisioning via SCIM.

choices.title: FND02-BP04: Establish controls to manage access based on lifecycle

helpfulResource.displayText: Joiner, mover, and leaver processes automatically adjust or revoke access, so permissions stay aligned with current role and employment status without manual intervention.

improvementPlan.displayText: Automate access revocation on offboarding via SCIM or HR system integration. Implement access reviews triggered by role changes. Audit accounts and permission sets for orphaned access on a regular cadence.

choices.title: FND02-BP05: Grant least privilege access

helpfulResource.displayText: Permissions default to least privilege and are refined continuously based on access that is actually used. IAM Access Analyzer and service control policies contribute to enforcement.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use IAM Access Analyzer to identify over-permissive policies. Enable permission boundaries for delegated role creation. Review policies using last-accessed data and trim permissions that have not been used within your defined window.

choices.title: FND02-BP06: Define permission guardrails for your organization

helpfulResource.displayText: Organization-wide SCPs and resource control policies act independently of individual permission grants, keeping controls consistent and preventing high-risk actions across all accounts.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define a baseline set of deny-list SCPs (e.g., restrict to approved Regions, prevent disabling security services, block root user API calls). Apply them at the root or appropriate OU level. Ensure security and audit accounts have equal or stricter guardrails.

choices.title: FND02-BP07: Implement data perimeter controls to prevent unintended access

helpfulResource.displayText: Resource-based policies and VPC endpoint policies ensure only trusted identities, resources, and networks within your organization can access sensitive data, regardless of individual permission grants.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement S3 bucket policies and AWS Organizations condition keys (aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:ResourceOrgID) to establish data perimeters. Use VPC endpoint policies to restrict S3 and other service access to organization-owned identities.

choices.title: FND02-BP08: Audit and rotate credentials periodically

helpfulResource.displayText: Long-lived credentials are inventoried, owned, and rotated on a known schedule. The number of long-lived credentials is minimized and each one has a documented owner.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use AWS Config rules to detect IAM access keys older than your rotation threshold. Automate rotation for service account keys using AWS Secrets Manager. Report on and remediate keys without documented owners.

choices.title: FND02-BP09: Establish a process to continually review and refine permissions

helpfulResource.displayText: Permission reviews happen on a defined cadence and produce actual reductions. Reviews are triggered by changes in role and are supported by last-accessed data rather than producing activity without outcome.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish a quarterly permission review cadence using IAM Access Analyzer and IAM last-accessed reports. Set a target to reduce average policy size each review cycle. Track and trend the number of overly permissive policies as a metric.

choices.title: FND02-BP10: Establish workload and machine identity federation

helpfulResource.displayText: Workloads and machines obtain short-lived credentials through IAM Roles or OIDC-based federation. Long-lived credentials for machine use are eliminated wherever federation is available.

improvementPlan.displayText: Replace static IAM access keys in CI/CD pipelines with OIDC federation. Assign IAM roles to EC2 instances, Lambda functions, ECS tasks, and EKS pods. Inventory any remaining long-lived machine credentials and create migration plans for each.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the identity and access management best practices are currently implemented.

questions.title: How do you establish consistent, centralized observability into your cloud resources across all accounts and Regions?
questions.description: Observability gives teams a shared, reliable view of how the cloud environment is behaving. Evaluate whether you have defined organization-wide standards and aggregated telemetry centrally across all accounts and Regions.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations – Central Observability Management (FND03)

choices.title: FND03-BP01: Define observability standards and policies

helpfulResource.displayText: Observability is a foundation capability with clear ownership, documented standards for log formats, metric namespaces, and trace sampling rates, and named accountability for telemetry quality across the organization.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define and publish organization-wide observability standards covering log format, retention, sampling rates, and metric naming conventions. Assign an owner accountable for telemetry quality. Enforce standards via IaC modules distributed through the service catalog.

choices.title: FND03-BP02: Establish central, cross-account observability capabilities

helpfulResource.displayText: Telemetry from every account is available through a shared cross-account view using Amazon CloudWatch cross-account observability or a third-party aggregation platform. Foundation, workload, and security teams operate from this shared view.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable CloudWatch cross-account observability or deploy a centralized observability account. Ensure new accounts are automatically enrolled via account provisioning automation. Instrument foundation components (networking, identity, shared security services) to the same standard as workloads.

choices.title: FND03-BP03: Establish centralized event monitoring and response

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Health events from every account are aggregated into a single organization-wide view and routed through automation so service issues and scheduled changes reach the teams that own the affected resources.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable AWS Health Organizational View in the management account. Configure Amazon EventBridge rules to forward all Health events to a central event bus and route them to the owning team via tags. Establish SLAs for responding to critical Health notifications.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the central observability management best practices are currently implemented.

questions.title: How do you maintain visibility, control, and governance over resources, configurations, and assets across accounts and Regions?
questions.description: Clear visibility and control over cloud resources is essential at scale. Evaluate whether you maintain authoritative inventory, enforce consistent tagging, provide curated shared patterns, manage patching and quotas centrally, and validate recovery through regular exercises.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations – Resource and Inventory Management (FND04)

choices.title: FND04-BP01: Implement standardized attribution policies

helpfulResource.displayText: Tagging is enforced at provisioning time, not applied by convention after the fact. Required tags are defined organization-wide and validated by tag policies and AWS Config rules.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define a mandatory tag schema (owner, environment, cost-center, application) and enforce it using AWS Organizations tag policies and Service Control Policies. Remediate existing untagged resources and report compliance as an ongoing metric.

choices.title: FND04-BP02: Establish an organization view of cloud inventory and dependencies

helpfulResource.displayText: The organization has a continuously maintained authoritative view of what exists, who owns it, and how resources depend on each other, without relying on manual collection or point-in-time snapshots.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable AWS Config aggregation across all accounts and Regions. Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory and AWS Service Catalog AppRegistry to map applications to resources. Build dashboards from the aggregated data to surface ownership and dependency information.

choices.title: FND04-BP03: Establish standard repositories of shared resources and patterns

helpfulResource.displayText: Common infrastructure is consumed from curated, versioned, security-vetted building blocks rather than rebuilt by each team, so the secure and compliant path is also the easiest path.

improvementPlan.displayText: Publish approved IaC modules (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK) to a central registry. Maintain an AWS Service Catalog with approved products. Keep modules discoverable, well-documented, and regularly updated to prevent teams from building alternatives.

choices.title: FND04-BP04: Implement mechanisms for patch management

helpfulResource.displayText: Patch management covers EC2, container images, AMIs, hybrid nodes, and serverless runtimes with both scheduled maintenance and an expedited path for zero-day vulnerabilities.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to enforce patch baselines across all EC2 and hybrid instances. Add container image scanning to CI/CD pipelines. Define and test an expedited patching runbook for critical CVEs with an SLA shorter than your normal window.

choices.title: FND04-BP05: Establish service quota management

helpfulResource.displayText: Service quotas are monitored organization-wide with proactive alerts, and DR Regions are sized for failover load rather than resting load, so workloads can scale when needed.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable AWS Service Quotas with CloudWatch alarms at 70-80% utilization thresholds. Pre-request quota increases in DR Regions based on failover capacity requirements. Review quota headroom as part of the account provisioning and workload onboarding process.

choices.title: FND04-BP06: Establish centralized backup standards and mechanisms

helpfulResource.displayText: Backups are managed centrally via AWS Backup, stored in isolated vaults with vault lock enabled, and held in a separate account from the data they protect so account-level compromise does not remove the recovery path.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define an organization-wide backup policy using AWS Backup and deploy it via AWS Organizations. Enable backup vault lock with WORM settings. Store backup vaults in a dedicated backup account. Run restore exercises on a regular schedule and record results.

choices.title: FND04-BP07: Establish cross-Region replication and failover capabilities

helpfulResource.displayText: Cross-Region resilience and shared services exist in multiple Regions with documented and tested failover procedures, rather than being asserted on paper and exercised only during a real incident.

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify all shared foundation services (DNS, Active Directory, logging, identity) and ensure they have multi-Region deployments. Document failover runbooks. Conduct scheduled failover drills and capture RTO/RPO metrics against your targets.

choices.title: FND04-BP08: Establish resilience testing tooling

helpfulResource.displayText: Recovery and resilience claims are validated by exercise rather than assertion, with restores, failovers, and fault-injection experiments run on a regular cadence and findings fed back into the shared patterns.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) to run scheduled chaos experiments on shared foundation services. Track experiment results and use them to update IaC modules and runbooks. Establish a game day cadence for multi-Region failover scenarios.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the resource and inventory management best practices are currently implemented.

questions.title: How do you detect, respond to, and remediate security threats and compliance violations?
questions.description: A strong security posture combines preventive, proactive, detective, and reactive controls. Evaluate whether your foundation provides emergency access, standardized telemetry, threat detection, vulnerability management, dedicated security tooling, forensic readiness, and centralized encryption and key management.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations – Security and Compliance (FND05)

choices.title: FND05-BP01: Shift compliance checks left with proactive controls

helpfulResource.displayText: Compliance rules are codified and enforced in pipelines, at provisioning time, and in provisioning services so non-compliant resources are blocked before they exist wherever practical.

improvementPlan.displayText: Integrate CloudFormation Guard, cfn-nag, or OPA policy checks into your CI/CD pipelines. Use AWS CloudFormation hooks or Service Control Policies to block non-compliant resource creation at provisioning time. Measure the ratio of detective-to-preventive findings and trend it toward prevention.

choices.title: FND05-BP02: Establish emergency access mechanisms

helpfulResource.displayText: Emergency access works independently of the primary identity path, is tightly monitored for misuse, and is exercised regularly enough to be trusted during a real failure.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement a break-glass process using root or dedicated IAM accounts stored in a separate secure vault, independent of your primary identity provider. Set up CloudWatch alarms and SNS notifications for any break-glass usage. Test the process quarterly.

choices.title: FND05-BP03: Configure audit logging of cloud operations

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS CloudTrail is enabled organization-wide with a trail that captures management and data events and writes to a central, protected S3 bucket in a dedicated log archive account.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable an organization-wide CloudTrail trail that writes to a log archive account with S3 Object Lock. Enable CloudTrail Insights for unusual API activity detection. Ensure the log archive account is accessible to security teams but locked from modification by workload accounts.

choices.title: FND05-BP04: Configure standardized locations for logs, traces, and metrics

helpfulResource.displayText: Audit logs, traces, metrics, and resource inventory are captured in standardized, centrally owned, immutable locations that support correlation, investigation, compliance evidence, and point-in-time reconstruction.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define and enforce standard log destinations (e.g., central S3 bucket, Security Lake) and retention policies organization-wide. Use VPC Flow Logs, DNS query logs, and CloudWatch Logs with cross-account subscription filters to route telemetry to central storage.

choices.title: FND05-BP05: Maintain an auditable cloud inventory record

helpfulResource.displayText: An up-to-date, queryable cloud inventory supports compliance evidence, security investigations, and change management without manual collection.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use AWS Config aggregation to maintain a continuously updated inventory across all accounts and Regions. Store configuration snapshots in a central S3 bucket. Build queries using AWS Config Advanced Queries or Amazon Athena to support compliance reporting.

choices.title: FND05-BP06: Remediate non-compliant resources

helpfulResource.displayText: Non-compliant resources have owned, prioritized response workflows with defined SLAs rather than sitting as unactioned findings in a backlog.

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure AWS Config auto-remediation rules for common violations. Route findings from AWS Security Hub to ticketing systems with severity-based SLAs. Report on mean time to remediation by finding type and severity as an operational metric.

choices.title: FND05-BP07: Implement threat detection mechanisms

helpfulResource.displayText: Continuous threat detection runs at organization scale across all accounts and Regions, with findings flowing into owned, prioritized response workflows rather than sitting unattended.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable Amazon GuardDuty organization-wide with a delegated administrator account. Configure GuardDuty findings to flow into Security Hub and then to your SIEM or ticketing system with named owners and response SLAs for each severity tier.

choices.title: FND05-BP08: Employ vulnerability and patch management controls

helpfulResource.displayText: Continuous vulnerability scanning covers all compute types (EC2, containers, Lambda) and findings are linked to remediation workflows with defined SLAs, including an expedited path for critical CVEs.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable Amazon Inspector organization-wide for EC2, ECR container images, and Lambda. Route critical and high findings to owners with an SLA of 7 days or less. Integrate Inspector findings into Security Hub for unified visibility.

choices.title: FND05-BP09: Establish security tooling for investigating incidents

helpfulResource.displayText: Security tools operate from dedicated security tooling accounts separated from workloads, provisioned ahead of any incident so the team is not assembling capability under pressure.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create a dedicated security tooling account separate from general administration. Pre-deploy investigation tools (e.g., Amazon Detective, Security Hub, Athena queries against CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs). Ensure the security team can access this account independently of compromised workload accounts.

choices.title: FND05-BP10: Prepare forensic capabilities

helpfulResource.displayText: A forensic account and runbooks exist ahead of any incident. The chain of custody process is documented, evidence collection is automated where possible, and the forensic path is tested before it is needed.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish a dedicated forensics account with automated EC2 snapshot isolation runbooks (via AWS Systems Manager Automation). Document and test the chain of custody process. Run tabletop and live forensic exercises at least annually.

choices.title: FND05-BP11: Establish encryption and key management standards

helpfulResource.displayText: Encryption keys, secrets, and certificates are managed through central services with documented ownership, rotation, and cross-account sharing patterns that workloads consume instead of reinventing.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define encryption standards (algorithms, key lengths, rotation periods) and enforce them via SCPs and AWS Config rules. Use AWS KMS with multi-Region keys for replicated data. Manage certificates centrally via AWS Certificate Manager Private CA. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the security and compliance best practices are currently implemented.

questions.title: How do you track, control, and optimize cloud spend across teams and workloads?
questions.description: Managing cloud spend requires detailed visibility, consistent attribution, effective tooling, good commercial agreements, outcome-based metrics, and smart commitment discount strategies. Evaluate whether your foundation provides the cost management capabilities that let all teams understand and act on the spend they own.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations – Cloud Financial Management (FND06)

choices.title: FND06-BP01: Configure detailed cost information sources

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) with resource-level granularity is configured and exported to a data store where teams can query it. The pipeline is set up early so historical data is available from the start of the cloud journey.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable the AWS Cost and Usage Report with hourly granularity and resource IDs, exported to S3 and queried via Amazon Athena or a third-party BI tool. Enable it at the management account level to capture consolidated usage. Ensure the export was enabled from the start; if not, document the gap in historical visibility.

choices.title: FND06-BP02: Standardize cost attribution categories

helpfulResource.displayText: Cloud spend is attributed consistently to business dimensions (teams, products, environments, cost centers, applications). Cost allocation tags are both applied and activated for billing, so attribution reports are complete.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define an organization-wide cost allocation tag taxonomy aligned to business dimensions. Activate all relevant tags in the Billing console. Enforce tagging at provisioning time via tag policies. Report on tag coverage and trend it to 100% for cost-bearing resources.

choices.title: FND06-BP03: Configure billing and cost management tools

helpfulResource.displayText: Budgets, forecasts, and anomaly detection have assigned owners and response cadences so unexpected spend is caught and acted on rather than discovered in the monthly bill.

improvementPlan.displayText: Configure AWS Budgets at account, service, and tag levels with alert thresholds and named owners. Enable AWS Cost Anomaly Detection with notification subscriptions. Establish a weekly cost review cadence with workload owners. Use AWS Cost Explorer for trending and forecasting.

choices.title: FND06-BP04: Optimize software licensing and third-party agreements

helpfulResource.displayText: Commercial agreements, licensing, and commitment-based discounts are governed centrally against consolidated organization-wide usage and rebalanced as workloads evolve.

improvementPlan.displayText: Centralize Bring Your Own License (BYOL) tracking using AWS License Manager. Review third-party tool agreements annually against value delivered, especially those priced as a percentage of spend. Renegotiate agreements that do not scale linearly with value as your cloud estate grows.

choices.title: FND06-BP05: Establish organizational metrics to track optimization efforts

helpfulResource.displayText: Cost efficiency is measured against business outcomes, so optimization decisions reflect the value delivered per unit metric (e.g., cost per transaction, cost per customer) rather than raw infrastructure spend.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define unit economics metrics (cost per active user, cost per transaction, cost per GB processed) for key workloads. Assign named owners to dashboards and establish a monthly review cadence. Track and trend unit costs over time as a signal of efficiency improvement.

choices.title: FND06-BP06: Build strategies for commitment discounts and volume-based pricing

helpfulResource.displayText: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances are purchased centrally against consolidated usage on well-understood, stable workloads, and are reviewed and rebalanced as the environment changes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use AWS Cost Explorer's Savings Plans and RI recommendations, scoped to consolidated organizational usage. Establish a governance process to review commitment coverage and utilization quarterly. Avoid committing resources that are likely to be rightsized or modernized within the commitment term.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the cloud financial management best practices are currently implemented.

questions.title: How do you design, secure, and centrally manage network connectivity across the enterprise?
questions.description: A strong networking foundation balances centralized governance with operational efficiency. Evaluate whether your network topology, protection controls, and DNS are designed, secured, and managed centrally with workload teams consuming them through self-service patterns.

helpfulResource.displayText: AWS Well-Architected Cloud Foundations – Networking and Connectivity (FND07)

choices.title: FND07-BP01: Define your network and connectivity strategy and centralized resources

helpfulResource.displayText: The network is designed as a single enterprise foundation with topology, IP address allocation, and hybrid connectivity governed centrally and sized for growth. Workload teams consume network resources through self-service IaC modules rather than provisioning independently.

improvementPlan.displayText: Define an organization-wide IP addressing plan with reserves for new Regions, acquisitions, and hybrid partners. Use AWS Transit Gateway for hub-and-spoke connectivity. Share VPCs centrally using AWS Resource Access Manager. Publish IaC modules for VPC and subnet patterns to your shared catalog.

choices.title: FND07-BP02: Implement centralized network protection controls

helpfulResource.displayText: Traffic flowing north-south, east-west, and to shared services passes through consistent protection and inspection controls so security posture does not depend on which team built the workload.

improvementPlan.displayText: Deploy AWS Network Firewall or a third-party NGFW centrally in an inspection VPC attached to the Transit Gateway. Use AWS Firewall Manager to push WAF, Security Group, and Network Firewall policies organization-wide. Establish a review cadence for firewall rules to prevent allow-list accumulation.

choices.title: FND07-BP03: Establish centralized DNS management

helpfulResource.displayText: DNS is operated as a shared service with uniform resolution, filtering, and failover behavior. Hosted zones have clear ownership and DNS remains resolvable through component and Region failures.

improvementPlan.displayText: Centralize DNS in a shared DNS account using Amazon Route 53 Resolver with inbound and outbound endpoints shared via AWS Resource Access Manager. Use Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall for filtering. Document zone ownership in tags and establish a renewal and certification management process to avoid domains lapsing to individuals.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the networking and connectivity best practices are currently implemented.
